paragraphs.text: Welcome to Hutta & Price Orthodontics — a Gahanna-based practice led by Dr. James T. Hutta and Dr. Jeffrey Price. paragraphs.text: Dr. James T. Hutta, D.D.S., M.S., leads diagnosis and treatment planning at the practice. A Columbus native, he graduated from The Ohio State University College of Biological Sciences and the Ohio State College of Dentistry, then completed a three-year orthodontic residency at the Eastman Dental Center, University of Rochester School of Medicine. Dr. Hutta has been practicing orthodontics since 1992 and focuses on combining proven techniques with modern technology to deliver comfortable, individualized care.

paragraphs.text: Here at Hutta & Price Orthodontics we recognize that every patient is unique and deserves orthodontic care tailored to their individual needs. We believe the best care begins the moment you walk through the door — with a warm welcome, compassionate staff, clear communication, and state-of-the-art technology to deliver efficient, comfortable, and lasting results. We put people first, encourage questions, and create personalized treatment plans so every patient leaves healthier and more confident.

We offer a variety of treatment options to meet each patient's goals, including traditional braces, Damon systems, and clear aligner therapy. Our team works with you to choose a plan that fits your lifestyle, timeline, and budget, and we explain each step so you feel informed and comfortable throughout treatment.

Through modern digital tools like intraoral scanning and advanced imaging, gentle clinical techniques, and flexible scheduling, we make quality orthodontic care achievable for everyone in our community. Our focus is on creating healthy, lasting smiles while making the experience as easy and positive as possible.
We measure success by more than straight teeth: we want patients who feel confident, well cared for, and excited to share their smiles with family and friends.

image.alt: Dr. James Hutta headshot

paragraphs.text: “There is no greater compliment than when a patient entrusts us with their smile. To honor this, our doctors have dedicated themselves to providing premier orthodontic care and transforming incredible smiles every day. With over 30 years of combined experience and a commitment to staying at the forefront of advancements, our team delivers thoughtful, individualized care.”

Dr. James Hutta has practiced orthodontics since 1992. He founded the practice to provide care rooted in compassion and modern techniques, and he takes pride in building long-term relationships with patients and families.

image.alt: Dr. James Hutta smiling in his office

paragraphs.text: Dr. Hutta graduated with honors from the Ohio State College of Biological Sciences and from the Ohio State College of Dentistry. He completed a three-year residency in orthodontics at the Eastman Dental Center, University of Rochester School of Medicine.

image.alt: Dr. James Hutta headshot

paragraphs.text: Originally from the Columbus area, Dr. Hutta enjoys spending time with family, travelling, and playing golf. He is an avid Buckeye and Blue Jackets fan and remains deeply involved in supporting local schools and community programs.
He values the sense of family at the practice and takes joy in getting to know patients personally while delivering high-quality orthodontic care.

image.alt: Dr. James Hutta portrait
Dr. Jeffrey Price headshot

paragraphs.text: “Orthodontics is truly my passion. Every day, I look forward to meeting new people and building relationships with my patients and their families. Helping people to achieve the beautiful smile they’ve always desired and feel confident about the way they look is one of the most rewarding parts of my job.”
Dr. Price has built his reputation on delivering high-quality, efficient orthodontic care paired with clear communication and personalized service.

image.alt: Dr. Jeffrey Price smiling in his treatment room

paragraphs.text: A Columbus native, Dr. Price graduated cum laude from Ohio Wesleyan University and earned his D.D.S. summa cum laude from The Ohio State University. He completed a 33‑month orthodontic residency at The Ohio State University and earned a Master of Science in Orthodontics.
Dr. Price is a Diplomate of the American Board of Orthodontics and is a member of the AAO, ADA, Ohio Dental Association, and the Columbus Dental Society.

paragraphs.text: Damon Braces use a modern self-ligating system that eliminates elastic ties, reducing friction and discomfort. The system moves teeth efficiently and can shorten treatment time while offering a clear-bracket option for a more discreet look.

image.alt: Consult with your orthodontist about clear brace options

paragraphs.text: Invisalign<sup>®</sup> straightens teeth with a series of clear, custom-made aligners. Treatment begins with a 3D scan to create a precise plan, then progress is made by switching aligners approximately every two weeks.

Aligners are removable for eating and oral hygiene, and their smooth design avoids the irritation often caused by wires. This makes Invisalign<sup>®</sup> an attractive option for adults and teens seeking discreet treatment.

image.alt: Clear aligners being demonstrated, what are clear aligners

paragraphs.text: Smile Touch-Up is a short-term clear aligner option designed for minor corrections. It uses in-office 3D scanning and modeling to create a streamlined plan with fewer appointments and a lower cost than full orthodontic treatment.
This approach is ideal for patients needing small adjustments, such as those who wore braces in the past but need a quick realignment, often completing treatment in about six months.

image.alt: Smile Touch-Up short-term aligner treatment image

paragraphs.text: Traditional metal braces remain a reliable and effective way to correct complex tooth and bite issues. Modern metal brackets are smaller and more comfortable than in the past, making them a strong choice for patients of all ages.

image.alt: Traditional metal braces treatment example

paragraphs.text: Clear braces use tooth-colored materials to blend with your smile while delivering the same reliable tooth movement as metal braces. They are a popular choice for teens and adults who want a subtler look during treatment.

image.alt: Clear or tooth-colored braces shown on smile

paragraphs.text: Insignia Braces are fully customized using advanced 3D planning so brackets and wires are tailored to your teeth. That precision can improve comfort and efficiency for many patients.

image.alt: Insignia custom braces insignia results image

paragraphs.text: Retainers are essential to keep your smile aligned after active treatment. We offer removable and fixed options and provide guidance on wear and care to protect your results long term.
With in-office 3D printing, we can quickly replace retainers and ensure a precise fit when replacement is needed.

image.alt: Patient holding an orthodontic retainer, retainers and post treatment care

paragraphs.text: Palatal expanders and other interceptive appliances help guide jaw growth during childhood. Using these tools at the right time can create space, improve bite development, and reduce the need for more invasive treatment later.
We recommend a first orthodontic check by age 7 so we can monitor development and intervene when early treatment will improve long-term outcomes.

image.alt: Child beginning orthodontic care, early interceptive treatment

paragraphs.text: Find answers to common questions about orthodontics and care.

Orthodontics is a specialized form of dentistry that focuses on the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of dental and facial abnormalities. Your family dentist will likely refer you to an orthodontist such as Hutta & Price Orthodontics should you be in need of specialized dental care.

image.alt: Section accent with blue graphic

paragraphs.text: An orthodontist is a dental specialist who has received two to three years of additional training and experience. Altogether, it takes about ten years of higher education to become a licensed orthodontist. Orthodontists straighten teeth, correct misaligned jaw structure, and improve the function of your smile. Together, Dr. Hutta and Dr. Price have 30 years of experience creating beautiful smiles, so you can feel confident that you’re with the right orthodontist when you come to our practice.

image.alt: Decorative accessibility graphic

accordion.header: What is the best age to visit the orthodontist?

paragraphs.text: Orthodontists tend to work with younger populations because that’s the best time in a person’s life to address orthodontic problems. Age seven is an ideal time for a child’s first orthodontic appointment because enough adult teeth have come in that we can begin to see the relationship of the teeth to the rest of the mouth and make a professional assessment.

However, orthodontists are trained to correct crooked or crowded teeth or misaligned jaw structure for a person at any age, so if you’d like to brighten your smile, schedule your complimentary consultation today.

image.alt: Patient forms banner with friendly dental office graphics

accordion.header: How can I take care of my teeth if I'm wearing braces or a retainer?

paragraphs.text: Always brush your teeth after every meal and floss at least once a day. Use toothpaste that contains fluoride to prevent cavities, and ask about a fluoride rinse if recommended by our team.

If you take out your retainer to eat, place it in its container and brush and floss after the meal. Keep your retainer clean by brushing it gently with a toothbrush and toothpaste, or soak it in denture cleaner as instructed by our office. Avoid high temperatures such as boiling water or putting the retainer in the dishwasher.
While wearing braces, avoid foods high in sugar and sticky, chewy items like hard candies or gum. Ask our team for a complete list of foods to avoid and other care tips.
Adhere to routine checkups with your family dentist, typically every six months, to help prevent cavities and maintain oral health during orthodontic treatment.

image.alt: Dental care and prevention graphic

accordion.header: If I get braces, how long do I have to wear them?

paragraphs.text: The amount of time spent in braces will vary from patient to patient, but the average amount of time is about 22 months.

image.alt: Decorative accessibility graphic

paragraphs.text: Braces can be uncomfortable at first as your mouth gets used to the orthodontic appliance, but they should not be painful. If you are experiencing severe pain with your braces, contact us as soon as possible.

image.alt: Patient forms banner with friendly dental office graphics

accordion.header: Will my braces interfere with my school activities like sports, playing an instrument, or singing?

paragraphs.text: It depends on what extracurriculars you’re involved in. You can still participate in events, but some activities may require extra care. For contact sports such as football or basketball, a mouthguard will help protect your braces and mouth.
